Last week’s firm-wide @smbcapital meeting was about better adapting to different market regimes.

Which begs the question - what types of market regimes are there for discretionary traders? And what playbooks should we be running for each of them?

I’ll start and you all can expand on this in the replies.

Obviously this is far from exhaustive and kept high-level, but I think this should lead serious traders to do some deep reflection of their own. 

1. Theme-driven bullish market. Markets like this one favor momentum strategies, swing longs, overnight momentum, IPOs, and headlines relevant to the driving theme.

Early summer of 2026 certainly fell under this with AI as the driver and leading sectors like DRAM / cloud computing.

2. Macro-driven markets. Think in the spring during the start of the U.S.-Iran conflict, think  2025 Trump tariffs and the Russia-Ukraine war. Due to the randomness and volatility of these headlines, this market highly favors breaking news trading as well as trading move-to-move, while greatly reducing overnight exposure and swing exposure. 

3. Range-bound market. Think of the last couple months, where we've had no prevailing theme and most indices have stayed range-bound while the leaders from the prior cycle corrected. text:
$META

META OFFICIALLY ENTERS THE CAPITAL RAISING GAME THROUGH SELLING MORE OF THEIR STOCK.

Meta announced plans to raise approximately $35 billion through two equity offerings:

- $22.5B in Class A common stock through forward sale agreements.

- $12.5B in depositary shares tied to mandatory convertible preferred stock.

The company is also considering a separate $60 billion offering program for its new nonvoting Class C shares, potentially beginning in Q1 2027. The nonvoting class was introduced on earnings last week and will result in a 2-for-1 stock split. 

The total raise so far will be around $95B, $10B more than Google’s $85B equity offering from a few months ago. 

$NVDA NVIDIA, $AMD, and $AVGO Broadcom have also expressed nonbinding interest in purchasing a combined $5 billion of Meta shares…which basically means the suppliers of chips to Meta will now be taking a direct equity stake into them. Meta already has warrants that convert into shares for 10% of $AMD if it holds above $600 in the future. 

Capital is now becoming the constraint…whoever can raise the most will win.

zh_summary: 回測不是為了證明你的策略有效。而是發現策略如何表現。它多久會虧損？連虧持續多久？大部分利潤從哪來？哪些市場環境會傷害它？對執行成本有多敏感？平均回報幾乎無法告訴你實際需要承受什麼才能賺到它。研究權益曲線的旅程，而不僅僅是最終數據的終點。
en_summary: Backtesting isn't about proving that your strategy works. It's about discovering how the strategy behaves. How often does it lose? How long can losing streaks last? Where do most profits come from? Which market environments hurt it? How sensitive is it to execution costs? An average return tells you surprisingly little about what you'll actually have to endure to earn it. Study the journey of the equity curve, not just the destination of the final data.
ko_summary: 백테스팅은 전략이 작동한다는 것을 증명하는 것이 아니다. 전략이 어떻게 행동하는지 발견하는 것이다. 얼마나 자주 지는가? 연패가 얼마나 지속될 수 있는가? 대부분의 이익은 어디서 오는가? 어떤 시장 환경이 해를 끼치는가? 실행 비용에 얼마나 민감한가? 평균 수익률은 실제로 그것을 얻기 위해 견뎌야 할 것을 거의 알려주지 않는다. 최종 데이터의 목적지뿐만 아니라 에퀴티 커브의 여정을 연구하라.

zh_summary: 現在每一美元都想進入AI計算。ARK Invest的Brett Winton解釋為什麼這使持有比特幣的「保險」更昂貴。世界正在發出巨大的緊急信號，要求資本進入AI計算基礎設施。任何無法立即產生巨大回報的資產看起來淨值更差。持有比特幣作為這份保險合約的成本上升了。這對所有企業都是問題。有一個黑洞將資金拉入超智能所需的基礎設施，考慮到數據中心的預期回報，池子裡的錢不夠。
en_summary: Every dollar wants to be in AI compute right now. ARK Invest's Brett Winton on why that's making Bitcoin's insurance more expensive to hold. The world is sending out a giant emergency beacon for capital into AI compute infrastructure. Any asset not generating immediate great returns looks net worse. The cost of holding Bitcoin for this insurance contract has gone up. It's an issue for all businesses. There's a black hole pulling money into infrastructure for superintelligence, and not enough money in the pool given prospective returns of data centers.
ko_summary: 지금 모든 달러가 AI 컴퓨팅에 들어가고 싶어한다. ARK Invest의 Brett Winton이 왜 이것이 비트코인 '보험' 보유 비용을 더 비싸게 만드는지 설명한다. 세계는 AI 컴퓨팅 인프라에 자본을 투입하라는 거대한 비상 신호를 보내고 있다. 즉각적인 큰 수익을 내지 않는 자산은 순 기준으로 더 나빠 보인다. 이 보험 계약을 위해 비트코인을 보유하는 비용이 상승했다. 이는 모든 비즈니스의 문제다. 초지능을 위한 인프라에 돈을 끌어들이는 블랙홀이 있으며, 데이터 센터의 예상 수익을 고려하면 풀에 돈이 충분하지 않다.
text:
Every dollar wants to be in AI compute right now

ARK Invest's Brett Winton on why that's making Bitcoin's "insurance" more expensive to hold

"Right now the world is basically sending out this giant emergency spinning beacon. All capital available needs to go into AI compute infrastructure, because we need as much as possible."

"Any asset that's not generating immediate great returns looks net worse on that basis. And so the cost of holding Bitcoin for this insurance contract has gone up."

"It's not just a Bitcoin and cryptocurrency issue. That is an issue for all businesses of all stripes all over the world."

"There's a black hole, and there's kind of like the tidal force that's pulling money into creating the infrastructure we need for superintelligence."

"Given the prospective returns of building data centers, it's clear that there's not enough money in that pool. And so it means that there's still this call on capital from everywhere else."

text:
AI isn't in its dot-com moment yet.

ARK Invest's Brett Winton says AI infrastructure still isn't getting enough funding despite high yields, because investors doubt the end demand

"In the dot-com era, it's kind of like everybody was worth a gazillion dollars, no matter the metrics underneath. I think there will be a point in this cycle where that happens here, but we're clearly not there yet."

"Before you can get to that state, you need everybody who has the contrary state to basically get fired or bankrupted. And we're not there yet."

"Imagine a fixed income manager, and they have some poor guy who is trying to invest in compute attached debt or chip attached debt, and the guy is saying, these things are dynamite. These are screaming yield producing buys that we should invest in."

"He has to convince his own internal team that he should get more resources. And they're saying, well, where's the end demand? And so, even though the yields are very high, he's not getting the resources that he should."

"And that takes time. It takes at least a few years. And so, as a result, you could have these extra normal returns in the AI infrastructure space."

ARK Invest's Brett Winton on why AI agents will almost inevitably need digital assets

"Previously, the difference between free and 5 cents was like an infinite difference in terms of your ability to actually get somebody to do something, because the cognitive burden of spending 5 cents is too high for the end user."

"But if the agent is sitting there with a balance of money that it can spend as it sees fit to provide you with what you need, that could be data, an incremental service."

"The agent's ability to do that frictionlessly means they have to have a pool of assets under their control, rather than having to go back to you for approval every time."

"You probably want to stage those assets in a way where you have a big pool of assets that's protected from the agent, where it needs permission, and a smaller pool that it can wrangle. And so then almost inevitably those have to be digital assets."

text:
That tracks with my experience. I've written 4 non-fiction books with my wife (who graduated summa cum laude with a degree in journalism) acting as primary editor.

The first thing she ever edited for me was a piece that Barron's published in 1992. I—having been the Editor-in-Chief of my High School newspaper and a long-time writer—thought the version I gave to her only needed a bit of polishing. 

What came back from her was a SEA of red ink with innumerable corrections and rewrites. 

I was livid! Not only was my ego crushed, I turned it into a huge fight with her, accusing her of trying to drain all of my wonderfully creative darlings out of the piece and replacing them with pedestrian prose for the sake of clarity. The fight got so heated we ended up not speaking about it for the rest of the day.

But then I dutifully went through my original draft and made all of the changes she recommended and the scales fell from eyes—her edited version of my original draft was VASTLY better than my draft. I immediately confessed this to her while simultaneously begging her to be the primary editor on the first book I wrote called "Invest Like the Best."

In hindsight, this was the best thing that could have ever happened to my writing career. Yes, I was emotionally wounded by the harsh criticism, but it was clearly needed. I'm of the opinion that ALL writers, no matter how gifted, could see their work materially improved by a gifted, honest to the point of inflicting emotional damage

Furthermore, the group sold -$1.0 billion in overseas short-term bonds in the week ending October 17th, marking their 2nd weekly sale over the last 3.

Year-to-date, sales of foreign debt by Japanese investors are up to -$33.0 billion, the largest outflow over the comparable period since 2022.

The global bond market is experiencing a historic shift in investor demand.

zh_summary: Elon Musk的雙面計算策略：租給對手，為Grok建造。ARK Invest的Brett Winton談SpaceX意外的13吉瓦計算目標（至27年底，從指引的5至10上調），有足夠電力和冷卻可達20。以短期合約承包數據中心。Musk為對手如Anthropic供應基礎設施，同時建立自己的資源。

ARK Invest's Brett Winton on SpaceX's surprise 13-gigawatt compute target by end of '27 (up from guided 5 to 10), with power and cooling for up to 20. Contracting data centers on short-term contracts. Musk supplying infrastructure for rivals like Anthropic while building his own.
ko_summary: Elon Musk의 양면 컴퓨트 전략: 경쟁자에게 임대하고 Grok을 위해 구축한다. ARK Invest의 Brett Winton은 SpaceX의 27년 말까지 13기가와트 컴퓨트 목표(가이드 5에서 10에서 상향)에 대해 언급하며, 최대 20까지 전력과 냉각이 가능하다. 데이터 센터를 단기 계약으로 계약한다. Musk는 Anthropic과 같은 경쟁자에게 인프라를 공급하면서 자신의 자원을 구축한다.
text:
Elon Musk's 2-sided compute strategy: rent to rivals, build for Grok.

ARK Invest's Brett Winton on SpaceX's surprise 13-gigawatt compute target, and how it's pulling the AI industry forward

"I anticipated that they, who had guided to like 5 to 10 gigawatts of compute by the end of '27, would be like, yeah, maybe 4 to 5 is where we're headed."

"Instead, they said, actually, we're going to get up to 13 gigawatts by the end of '27, and we have enough power and cooling available that we could get to 20."

"They're contracting out their data centers on short-term contracts rather than having to line up a long-term contract against their build."

"Elon Musk's mania is supplying the infrastructure that at least Anthropic needs to deliver these services and improvements of services into the future."

"He's both empowering his rival, but also building up the resource he needs to catch up to his rival."
